import re, sys

def remove(path, names):
    lines = open(path).read().split('\n')
    for name in names:
        # locate the declaration line
        idx = None
        pats = [
            re.compile(r'^func\s+' + re.escape(name) + r'\s*\('),
            re.compile(r'^func\s+\([^)]*\)\s+' + re.escape(name) + r'\s*\('),
            re.compile(r'^type\s+' + re.escape(name) + r'\s+struct'),
        ]
        for i, l in enumerate(lines):
            if any(p.match(l) for p in pats):
                idx = i
                break
        if idx is None:
            print(f'  !! NOT FOUND: {name} in {path}')
            sys.exit(1)
        start = idx
        # absorb contiguous preceding comment lines
        while start > 0 and lines[start-1].startswith('//'):
            start -= 1
        # find closing brace at column 0
        end = idx
        while end < len(lines) and lines[end] != '}':
            end += 1
        if end >= len(lines):
            print(f'  !! NO CLOSE: {name} in {path}')
            sys.exit(1)
        # absorb one trailing blank line
        stop = end + 1
        if stop < len(lines) and lines[stop].strip() == '':
            stop += 1
        # if we are now at EOF-ish, also drop a preceding blank
        removed = stop - start
        del lines[start:stop]
        print(f'  removed {name}: {removed} lines from {path}')
    open(path, 'w').write('\n'.join(lines))

if __name__ == '__main__':

Four agents ran; all four converged on the same finding, which I verified myself before acting.

## Applied

**The session-entry model was dead and I'd left it standing.** `AgentSession.Entries`, `SessionEntry`, `EntryType` and its four constants existed *only* to be read by the four methods the first commit deleted — so removing those methods orphaned the data shape. Nothing populated it: I checked every `AgentSession` construction site (all ten agents, plus `resume.go` and `strategy/manual_commit_pending.go`). The three surviving references were tests asserting that a struct literal reads back, which the compiler already guarantees.

Second commit: **75 more lines gone**, total 637. Build, vet, lint (0 issues) and full `test:ci` exit 0. Pushed.

One thing that changes my earlier report: I'd flagged this in the PR body as a product judgment call for a human, on the strength of the field's comment offering it as an extension point ("agents may populate this if needed"). That defense doesn't survive checking — `AgentSessionJSON`, the external plugin wire format, has **no entries field**, so an out-of-tree agent can't populate it either. It was never wired up as an extension point. I took it and rewrote that section of the PR body rather than leaving a stale "deliberately not decided" claim standing.

## Skipped, with reasons

- **`GetSessionID` / `ReadSession` on the interface.** The altitude agent quantified what I'd only asserted: implemented 10×, invoked through `agent.Agent` 0× (vs. `WriteSession` 2 call sites, `FormatResumeCommand` 4). Right-altitude fix is moving them off the base interface — but they back the `get-session-id` / `read-session` verbs of the external plugin protocol, so that's a contract change, not a cleanup. Reported as facts in the PR.
- **Doc drift.** `docs/architecture/claude-hooks-integration.md` step 5 still describes `FindCheckpointUUID` "used for rewind linking". I didn't patch it: that section already documents an architecture that doesn't exist — `handlePostTask`, `TaskCheckpointContext`, `SaveTaskCheckpoint` all have zero hits in the tree. Fixing the one line my diff invalidated would make a wholesale-stale section look maintained. Noted in the PR as deserving its own pass.
- **Reuse and efficiency: no findings.** No duplicate remnants survive, and the shared `transcript` package deliberately doesn't model `tool_result` blocks, so there was nothing to fold the deleted helper into — the deletion was correctly scoped, not a half-refactor.

## Two notes

I nearly reported a false negative: my first verification grep used `\b` word boundaries, which `git grep -E` silently doesn't support here — it matched nothing and looked like confirmation. That's the same trap already in my notes for `\s`; I've been treating it as `\s`-specific and it isn't.
